blocks.text: This page tracks the Port Moody MLS® Home Price Index benchmark for October 2026: $995,800 for a typical home, down 6.6% over twelve months.
Port Moody benchmark prices and trends, October 2026

A typical Port Moody home carried an MLS® Home Price Index benchmark of $995,800 in October 2026. That is down 1.6% on the month, down 4.4% over three months, down 3.2% over six months and down 6.6% over the year. Over three years it is down 11.3%, and over five years down 2.6%.
The weakest one-year move in Port Moody was for a townhouse homes at −10.1%; the strongest was an apartment at −3.7%.
The gap between a detached home ($1,868,000) and an apartment ($680,000) is $1,188,000, and a townhouse ($895,800) sits $215,800 above the apartment benchmark.
Against Greater Vancouver, where the all-home benchmark was $1,068,600, Port Moody is 6.8% below. Over the year Greater Vancouver moved down 5.2% against down 6.6% here.
Of the 20 areas this board reports, Port Moody ranks 11 by all-home benchmark, with Richmond above it at $998,300 and Burnaby South below it at $975,400.

Detached homes in Port Moody: benchmark $1,868,000, down 1.9% in a month, down 5.1% in three months, down 3.5% in six months, down 9.3% in a year, down 9.8% in three years and little changed at +0.5% in five. That is 5.2% above the detached benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,775,200).

Townhouse homes in Port Moody: benchmark $895,800, down 4.8% in a month, down 8.9% in three months, down 6.8% in six months, down 10.1% in a year, down 13.0% in three years and little changed at −0.4% in five. That is 11.0% below the townhouse benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($1,006,500).

Apartment homes in Port Moody: benchmark $680,000, little changed at +0.6% in a month, little changed at −1.2% in three months, down 3.3% in six months, down 3.7% in a year, down 8.1% in three years and up 3.5% in five. That is 1.0% above the apartment benchmark for Greater Vancouver ($673,400).

blocks.text: In dollars, the typical Port Moody home is worth about $70,400 less than in October 2025, when the benchmark was near $1,066,200. By type, detached homes lost about $191,500, from $2,059,500 to $1,868,000, townhouses lost about $100,600, from $996,400 to $895,800, and apartments lost about $26,100, from $706,100 to $680,000 over those twelve months. Further back, the benchmark was near $1,028,700 six months ago and near $1,122,700 three years ago, so today's figure sits about $32,900 below the six-month mark and about $126,900 below the three-year mark. Against Greater Vancouver, the Port Moody benchmark is about $72,800 below the regional $1,068,600; a year earlier the difference was about $61,000 below.
What the Port Moody figure is
The $995,800 Port Moody figure is a modelled price for a typical home, not a median, and it comes from Greater Vancouver REALTORS® for October 2026.
